notes: psymetadata documents the data only: 67 standardized mean differences of red vs a control color on test performance, study_id (22 per the page) and es_id one per row. Gnambs (2020, Psychon Bull Rev 27:1374-1382; PMC7704521, method read): the effect sizes were pooled using a random-effects model with REML in metafor, and because some studies provided more than one effect size, a multivariate meta-analysis was specified that acknowledged the sampling covariances (Gleser and Olkin); tau^2 is reported between the 38 independent samples, which have no column, so study_id (the publication holding them) stands in. Moderators were the control color, color matching, presentation and the cognitive measure. vi is the sampling variance, which the source weights by. Hand check #162: the author's code (osf.io/eb9yv) fits rma.mv on the 67 effects with random = ~ 1 | sno, the independent sample, and the sampling covariance matrix V; the table omits sno (22 study_id labels), so the study and effect intercepts stay the reader's proposal, published_model no.

psymetadata documents the data only (OSF ux3eh): a subset of Many Labs 2 (Klein et al. 2018, Adv Methods Pract Psychol Sci), one effect per replicating lab (lab) and replicated finding (analysis), in r (yi_r, vi_r) and in d (yi_d, vi_d, the same effect on another scale). The paper meta-analyses each finding across samples (not read here), so rows repeat within lab across findings, crossed; lab is rendered as a random intercept and the finding as a covariate. Lab-level moderators: country, weird, western, educated, industrialized, rich, democratic, mean_weird_score, online. vi_r is the sampling variance, which the source weights by. The per-finding fits treat the labs as independent; the lab is counted as a cluster, published_model no. Hand check #162: stands as a cluster the source treats as independent counts; 114 of the 115 labs hold several of the 25 findings.

psymetadata documents the data only (OSF fq5wp): 2,443 Fisher-z effects from 131 meta-analyses of intelligence research, study_id the primary study's label (first author or sample), es_id the effect, es and se the effect on its original scale (type_es). Nuijten et al. (2020, J Intell 8:36; PMC7720125, method read): a two-step strategy, a random-effects meta-regression on the standard error within each meta-analysis with rma() in metafor (Paule-Mandel), then a random-effects meta-analysis of the per-meta-analysis coefficients; a multilevel model of primary studies nested in meta-analyses was tried but failed to converge (footnote 2). Proposed: the effects grouped by their primary study's label. vi is the sampling variance, which the source weights by. Hand check #162: study_id codes the source file's author_andor_study label (osf.io/cysa9): 1,917 labels of 1 to 14 effects, 343 with several, 151 of them across meta-analyses. The meta-analysis (ma, 131 levels) has no column in this table, so the effects cannot nest in it; published_model stays no.

psymetadata documents the data only (PsyArXiv gjqcs): 99 Hedges' g effects of executive function in intellectual disability vs mental-age-matched controls from 26 studies (study_id), es_id one per row, group_id the aetiology (NSID, FXS, DS, WS), ef_type, ef_component, domain and test. Spaniol and Danielsson (2022, J Intellect Disabil Res 66:9-31; PubMed abstract): a multilevel random-effects meta-analysis, g = -0.34, aetiology a significant moderator; effects nested in studies. vi is the sampling variance, which the source weights by. Hand check #162: stands; the preprint's method (PsyArXiv gjqcs) adds a random effect per study to the one per effect size, after Assink and Wibbelink (2016). Its moderator fits (aetiology, EF component, domain) have the same response and grouping, so they file no row.

psymetadata documents the data only (OSF szfwx): 76 correlations of learning goal orientation with performance adaptation from 35 studies (study_id), es_id one per row; stasielowicz2019b holds the performance goal orientation effects. Stasielowicz (2019, J Res Pers 82:103847; abstract via search): three-level meta-analyses were conducted for learning goal orientation and performance goal orientation, rendered as effects nested in studies. age_imputed fills age. vi is the sampling variance, which the source weights by; n enters it. Hand check #162: stands; the author's code (osf.io/wz8c7) fits rma.mv with random = ~ 1 | ID/Effect_ID by REML, ID the study_id of the source data (35 levels, 3.1 and 3.2 two samples of one paper) and Effect_ID unique per row. Its moderator and Egger fits have the same response and grouping, so they file no row.

psymetadata documents the data only (OSF szfwx): 86 correlations of performance goal orientation with performance adaptation from 28 studies (study_id), es_id one per row, pgo_type the goal orientation (avoid, prove, global); stasielowicz2019a holds the learning goal orientation effects. Stasielowicz (2019, J Res Pers 82:103847; abstract via search): three-level meta-analyses for learning and performance goal orientation, rendered as effects nested in studies. age_imputed fills age. vi is the sampling variance, which the source weights by; n enters it. Hand check #162: the author's code (osf.io/7xdkh) fits rma.mv with random = ~ 1 | ID/Effect_ID by REML on all 86 effects, then per pgo_type and with pgo_type as moderator, the later moderator analyses on the Avoid subset; these fits have the same response and grouping, so they file no row.

formula: rides ~ user + temp_actual + weekend + humidity + weather_cat + (1 | date)
notes: Help page: daily observations, 267 each for registered and casual riders, so each date holds two rows. Bayes Rules! Chapter 11 (chapter-11) plots rides against temp_actual, weekend, humidity and weather_cat by user and splits the table by user (filter(user == 'casual')), fitting no model on it. Proposed: a Poisson model of rides by user type and the day's weather, date the grouping factor of the paired rows (a column that indexes a unit the rows repeat within, #133). Days from the UCI Bike Sharing data (Fanaee-T and Gama 2013). Hand check #162: stands; 267 dates of two rows each.

RESPONSE INFERRED: the help page documents late-December Ontario counts of each species per year (1921-2017), one row per species and year, with no model. Bayes Rules! fits Normal, Poisson and Negative Binomial regressions only on its one-species subsets (bald_eagles in Exercises 12.5-12.9, loons). Proposed: the count with the person-hours as exposure and a species intercept. species_latin aliases species; count_per_hour and count_per_week are the count over hours. Hand check #162: stands; 199 species of 94 years each, the count varying within 194.

Bayes Rules! Exercise 16.2 (chapter-16, hierarchical models without predictors) asks whether farm_name and processing_method are grouping variables or predictors in a model of total_cup_points; batches repeat within farms, so farm_name groups. Exercise 17.14 (chapter-17) asks for a hierarchical model of total cup points over 'multiple batches from each of 27 farms' on coffee_ratings_small, a simplified version of this table excluded as derived, and leaves the predictors to the reader. Proposed: the one-way model of Chapter 16. total_cup_points sums the grades aroma to sweetness with clean_cup and a cupper score not in the table (CQI scoring), so the grades nearly determine it. Hand check #162: stands; 571 farms, 133 with several batches. species, Exercise 18.1's response, takes one value within every farm, so its farm model files no row.

Help page: one row per respondent of the popvssoda.com volunteer survey with the respondent's state and census region; pop marks the respondents whose word_for_cola is pop, so word_for_cola is ignored as the response's source. Bayes Rules! uses the table to illustrate Bayes' rule over regions and fits no model on it. Proposed: a logistic model with region and a state intercept; states nest in regions (an area factor with many levels groups, LGAclaims). Hand check #162: exhaustive areas group (ACS's states), so state stands against the outside check's design factor; pop varies within all 51 states (the District of Columbia among them), 574 to 32,017 respondents each.

formula: is_canceled ~ lead_time + previous_cancellations + is_repeated_guest + average_daily_rate + (1 | agent)
notes: Help page: a random 1,000 of the hotel bookings of Antonio, de Almeida and Nunes (2019, Data in Brief 22:41-49), one row per booking. Bayes Rules! Exercises 13.6-13.9 (chapter-13) fit a logistic regression of is_canceled on lead_time, previous_cancellations, is_repeated_guest and average_daily_rate, without grouping. agent holds the ID of the travel agency that made the booking: 118 agencies of 1 to 267 bookings, 63 with several, is_canceled varying within 37; the 128 bookings without an agency share the level NULL, kept as stored. Proposed: the exercises' model with an agency intercept. company is a second agency ID, NULL on 951 bookings; reservation_status and its date restate the response. Hand check #162: the exclusion found grouped by agent.
